hypotheses.justification: `NeZero N` is never needed: none of the definitions appearing in the statement demand it. `x1FunctionField M` (`Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_X1.lean`, line 137) is `x1FunctionFieldC ℚ M = qExpFunctionFieldC ℚ (Gamma1 M)`, and Mathlib's `Gamma1 (N : ℕ)` (`CongruenceSubgroups.lean`, line 132) is defined for every `N` (no `[NeZero N]`; only `Gamma1_is_congruence`/`instFiniteIndexGamma1` take `[NeZero N]`, and neither is used by `qExpFunctionFieldC`, which is just `IntermediateField.adjoin K (intFormRatiosC K Γ)`). `laurentBaseChange` (`Def_ModularCurve_LaurentCoeff.lean`, line 103), `x1FunctionFieldBar`, `JOne` and `Pic0`/`Pic0.torsion` (`Def_AlgebraicCurve_DivisorClassGroup.lean`, lines 223 and 244) are all defined without any `NeZero` assumption on the level; the `NeZero` instance relevant to `W`'s type is the one on `n`, supplied by the separate `[NeZero n]` binder in `DivisorialWeilPairingData` (`Def_AlgebraicCurve_FunctionFieldWeilPairingDivisorial.lean`, line 448). The Galois action on `JOne N` used in `hyσ`/`hx` comes from the instances in `Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean` (lines 90, 97), which are stated for an arbitrary base field `F₀` and thus also for arbitrary `N`. The proof itself never mentions `N`'s nonzeroness: the only `NeZero` it uses is the one on `n` (in `pair_nsmul_left`/`pair_zero_left`/`pair_ne_zero`). Hence deleting `[NeZero N]` leaves the statement well formed and true for every `N : ℕ` (including `N = 0`, where the statement is if anything degenerate but still holds by the very same argument), and the same proof goes through verbatim.
